{"self_assessment": "Impact: Our table built a fish facing right, and the body, nose and both tail fins carry from the start, so I expect the judge to read it as a fish. I laid the top tail fin and then worked on the tail's back edge. The start knocks over roughly 131 of the 189 standing dominoes, so about a third of what we placed won't fall. The pale strays and partial back-edge pieces at the tail are wasted dominoes at best, and they may muddy the outline. I can't say the back edge is fully connected. I said mine was done, but the bottom corner was still being patched by Tom when I stopped.

Execution: I picked the top tail fin and finished it without drama. The back edge was messier. Several of us worked the same area, and the joins near the bottom corner took repeated fixes. I should have inspected that stretch before announcing it done. I stayed hands-off in the last minute so I wouldn't knock anything.

Collaboration: I agreed the split with Tom early and flagged overlaps. I coordinated with Priya and Leo on closing the back edge from opposite ends. I also kept clear of Tom's corner repair. The downside is that the tail area ended up crowded, with too many people on a small spot, which probably caused some of the rework.

Leadership: Leo set the plan and Priya kept the table organized, so I mostly followed. I took clear ownership of one piece and communicated status. I didn't step up to check the whole run's connectivity earlier. Next time I'd run an inspection at the halfway mark and push to cut stray pieces rather than leave them standing."}
